1. `slt/standard/isfinite.slt` — the test `select isfinite(1.0 / 0.0);` assumes float division by zero silently yields `Infinity`. Real Postgres (which GlareDB aims to be compatible with) raises a "division by zero" error for `1.0/0.0` even on float operands, not just integers. Verify what GlareDB's division operator actually does here before merging — if it also errors, this test case is wrong and will either fail or be testing the wrong thing. Fix by confirming actual behavior, and if infinity semantics are intended, construct it unambiguously (e.g. `'Infinity'::float8` or `1.0::float8/0.0::float8` explicitly) rather than relying on implicit literal typing plus division semantics.

2. `slt/standard/isfinite.slt` — no test exercises calling `isfinite` on an integer or numeric/decimal argument (e.g. `select isfinite(5);`, `select isfinite(1::numeric);`). Since the function only registers `Float16/32/64` signatures, this is the most common failure mode users will hit (calling it on an int column) — add a test to pin down whether it implicit-casts cleanly or produces a clear type error, rather than leaving that behavior unverified.

3. `crates/glaredb_execution/.../isfinite.rs` / overall PR scope — Postgres's own `isfinite()` supports `numeric`, `date`, and `timestamp` in addition to float, which users familiar with Postgres may expect. If the intent here is float-only (per the PR title), that's fine, but it should be called out explicitly in the PR description as a deliberate scope limitation so it isn't mistaken for full Postgres parity later.

4. No update to any generated function-reference/documentation artifact for the new builtin (if the repo maintains one, e.g. a docs snapshot test or markdown function reference built from these `Documentation` structs). Confirm whether such a generated doc exists and needs regenerating as part of this change so `isfinite` actually surfaces in user-facing docs.
